Subject: Order form redline — SKU bundling / discount language

Hannah —

Thanks for the draft order form. Attached is our redline (PDF) with three areas we need clarity on:

1) SKU unbundling: We removed the clause that allows Redwood to bundle features into a single SKU without changing pricing. We need an explicit commitment that SKU composition and list price for a given SKU are stable within a 90-day notice window.

2) Discount tie-ins: We struck language that ties volume discounts to a combined "platform usage" metric that includes Embeddings + Generation. We propose separate discount bands per unit (tokens vs embedding units).

3) True-up and runoff: The redline introduces a pro-rata runoff for unconsumed committed units in the final 30 days if services are migrated.

We attached suggested alternative wording. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept any of these or propose counter language. We need this finalized for our procurement review next Tuesday.

Attachments: Orbifold_OrderForm_Redline.pdf

Regards,
Sarah Kim
Senior Procurement Manager
Orbifold AI

Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 11:30:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form redline — SKU bundling / discount language

Sarah — thanks for the redline and the clear ask. Appreciate the timeline.

Quick response on each:
- SKU composition: we understand the request for stability. We can commit to a 60-day notice to change SKU packaging for existing SKUs, and we can add a "migration assistance" clause to avoid surprise cost impact during transitions.
- Discount bands: separating discounts by unit type is reasonable; our pricing workbook has historically treated combined usage for tiering. I will loop in legal to draft alternative language that preserves band economics but supports separate bands where required.
- True-up/runoff: we need to protect against stranded reserved capacity on our side. Proposal: pro-rata runoff subject to a maximum of 30% of the committed month in the final 30 days unless a migration window >60 days is agreed.

Next steps: internal sync (low-touch) today — Marissa will propose wording; Ben/Irene will confirm commercial impact and whether we can accept the 60-day SKU notice. We will return a consolidated counter by EOD Monday (Aug 17) to meet your procurement timeline.

I'll attach our pricing workbook for transparency.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales — Enterprise

Subject: RE: internal — suggested counter language for Orbifold redline

Team —

I reviewed Orbifold's redline and drafted a focused counter. Key points below; full suggested text is in the attached snippet.

1) SKU stability clause (proposed):
- "Redwood will provide no less than sixty (60) days' prior written notice before materially changing the composition or pricing of any existing SKU. For changes that would materially increase Customer cost, Redwood will provide a migration path (fee amortization or transition credits) agreed in good faith.
"
2) Discount bands (proposed):
- Keep existing combined-tier economics but allow for an election once per term to opt into separate per-unit discount bands. This preserves our expected ARR while giving customers a path to per-unit stacking if they prefer.

3) Final period runoff (proposed):
- "If Customer terminates or migrates services, Customer is eligible for a pro-rata refund of prepaid/committed units for the final billing month subject to a maximum refund equal to thirty percent (30%) of that month's committed units, unless Customer provides at least sixty (60) days' written notice prior to termination. Refunds will not apply to usage consumed or to committed units already consumed by ancillary services.
"
Commercial impact: Ben — rough math says a 60-day SKU notice and the migration credit language would reduce near-term friction with large procurement teams but could increase churn risk if large customers exercise the election to split bands. Irene — please confirm whether the election frequency (once per term) is acceptable from a sales ops and forecasting perspective.

If we agree, I'll prepare a single tracked counter redline PDF for Hannah to send back to Orbifold.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order form redline — SKU unbundling and discount tie-ins (consolidated counter)

Sarah / John —

Thanks again for the redline and for flagging the procurement timing. We've reviewed internally and attached a consolidated counter redline (PDF) and a cleaned pricing workbook that maps the band math to both combined and per-unit views. High level:

- SKU changes: We can accept a 60-day notice commitment (see Section 3.2) and will include migration assistance language to mitigate customer impact.
- Discount tie-ins: We propose maintaining combined-tier economics by default but will allow customers one election per 12-month term to opt into separate per-unit discount bands (Section 4.1). The attached workbook shows modelling for both approaches.
- Final period runoff: We propose the pro-rata refund capped at 30% of the final month's committed units unless Customer provides >=60 days notice; refunds exclude already-consumed ancillaries (Section 7.4).

Attachments: Orbifold_OrderForm_Redline.pdf (tracked changes), RIF_pricing_workbook_v3.xlsx
